instruction: I trashed a poster file for a party by accident on my Ubuntu system. Could you help me get it back from the Trash?

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

result.command: [ -f /home/user/Desktop/poster_party_night.webp ] && echo 'File exists.' || echo 'File does not exist.'

metadata.explanation: Ubuntu-specific trash recovery with conversational tone. Evaluator confirms file back on Desktop using shell test.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies the instruction requirement: file restoration from trash to Desktop
Getter logic is semantically correct: uses shell file test [ -f ] to check existence at /home/user/Desktop/poster_party_night.webp
Metric comparison is appropriate: exact_match for binary file existence check
Expected value is correct: 'File exists.\n' matches the shell command output format
Data flow is complete: setup trashes file → user restores → evaluator checks file exists at original location
No postconfig needed: file system check doesn't require UI state or dialog reopening
Edge cases handled: shell test correctly differentiates between file exists vs. doesn't exist
